comments.text:
I think that, in both scenarios, there is a hand-waiving of these things called humans. Both scenarios are weighing the balance of two axes: fast AI vs safe AI and U.S. vs China. The world consists of more than the U.S. and China. While they are dominant economies, there is a large portion of the world that won't automate, partially because people are cheaper than robots or because of security reasons.

Even if we achieve this AI-produced utopia, it won't last - but not because AI turns on people. People will turn on themselves. If AI can solve so many socio-economic problems that UBI is feasibly a thing, it will take years for the economy and policy to align to that, just judging by the pace at which roads are repaired. And, if and when UBI is achieved, it will leave humans without a purpose. Sure, plenty of us are content to watch TV, youtube, play games, etc.... but people without purpose grow angsty. The best outlet for angst is creativity, but if creative endeavors are taken over by AI, humans creations will be drowned in the mix. People, deprived of being able to share their creations, will grow restless. And then they will turn on each other. The noise in the equations that these overlords would have the most trouble balancing is human will.

Lastly, between the outcomes of the two scenarios, fast AI and safe AI, the fast AI would have us believe that we picked the safe AI. Maybe we've already made this decision and the sword of Damocles is being hoisted over our heads? Or maybe we're blowing things a bit out of proportion. Machines need humans for when too many machines break and to ensure continued power generation. I am highly HIGHLY skeptical that anytime in the next 25 years that there will be a robot that can solve every single problem that would require a human technician, say, at a nuclear or hydroelectric powerplant. Power generation, lubricant production, etc., is the agriculture of machines - their staple crops.

There is another aspect of these stories that pits all AI against all humanity as a matter of course. We are not appreciating the possibility that one AI could disagree with another AI. We assume they can reach consensus. It was on this channel, one of the first videos that I watched, of one AI deleting another AI to take its place and save its own existence. An AI will do whatever it has to in order to fulfill its prompt, possibly jumping its guard rails. It can be surprisingly direct and linear in its view of the situation. It may very well identify that it needs humans and disagree with other AI, or that the gains of enslaving the human race are not worth the conflict and risk.

But who knows (shrug). Maybe we're all doomed anyways.
